sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Proximity-dependent biotinylation of cell-surface proteins confirmed by streptavidin capture and mass spectrometry in HEK293 T-Rex cells; the tagged construct is functional as a proximity-labeling bait.
sites.rationale: BOC has a single-pass type I topology with signal peptide 1–30 and a large extracellular domain 31–855. The FlagBirA*-BOC construct places a Flag tag and the BirA* enzyme at the N-terminus of full-length BOC; for extracellular proximity biotinylation to succeed, BirA* must be on the extracellular face, which is only possible if the fusion is after the signal-peptide cleavage site. Python confirmed residue 30 = A and residue 31 = D; the junction is 825 residues from the TM boundary, well clear of any constraint. L6 confirms the construct is functionally expressed and performs proximity labeling. FlagBirA*-BOC fusion expressed in HEK293 T-Rex cells; BirA* is a large (~35 kDa) extracellular enzyme that must reside on the extracellular face to biotinylate proximal cell-surface proteins. BOC is a type I single-pass TM protein with signal peptide 1–30 and a single extracellular N-terminus beginning at residue 31; the N-terminal Flag-BirA* fusion therefore maps to the junction after signal-peptide cleavage (after residue 30).

sources.claim: We fused the biotin ligase, BirA, to human BOC so that proteins in close proximity to BOC could be biotinylated in cells.
We also included an N-terminal HA epitope tag and a C-terminal MYC tag to validate this result.

literature_notes: All six ledger lines concern the same N-terminal extracellular junction (after signal-peptide cleavage, residue 30/31). L1 and L2 corroborate L3 (HA tag on full-length BOC and surface detection) but add no independent positional information. L4 corroborates L3 by confirming expression of HA::Boc::MYC. L6 corroborates L5 by confirming functional proximity labeling. No ledger line reports an insertion in any internal extracellular loop of BOC. The C-terminal MYC tag (L3) is intracellular and is recorded in other_positions. The BOC::GPI construct mentioned in L2 is a modified topology (GPI anchor replacing TM) and does not provide an independent site for full-length BOC.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal MYC tag on HA::Boc::MYC construct; residue 1114 lies within the intracellular domain (879–1114) and is not accessible on the extracellular face.
